messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPEN — p99 token latency > 1.5s (SLO 0.8s) for canary rollout `model-redwood-5b-v5` in us-west-2. Streaming stalls reported. Auto-alerting oncall: @raj. Dash: https://dash.redwood.internal/incident/1895001234 :rotating_light:

maya: saw it spike ~11:02 PDT, looks correlated with the v5 canary traffic shift. p95 up ~400ms, p99 up ~1.2-2.2s depending on seq len. some streaming sessions show stalls mid-response.

raj: I'm oncall, investigating. grabbing traces and KV cache hit rates. can someone snapshot the rollout config? @deploy-bot any recent changes?

deploy-bot: Deploy log: canary rollout initiated by @emma at 10:45 PDT -> 5% traffic to model-redwood-5b-v5 (quantized q4_0). No infrastructure scale events. Commit: d3f2a7c.

emma: I bumped canary to 5% to start perf tests. No runtime config changes. Rolling back is an option if we see sustained p99 > SLO.

leo: throwing up a couple of quick checks: KV cache miss rate for the canary pods is ~38% (normal ~10%), CPU on canary gpus around expected, memory ok. Batching latency per call is higher — backlog spikes at 50ms -> 200ms. streaming sinks show connection stalls ~150-300ms where clients see no tokens.

raj: interesting — cache miss spike could explain regen of KV and heavier compute causing tail. what's the model sequence length distribution for failing requests?

maya: initial look: failing tails skew long: 60% of p99s have seq len > 1024 and use tool-calling streams. Also noticed increased prefix mismatch rate from prefix-caching metrics (maybe different tokenizer behavior with v5 quantization).

raj: plan: 1) pause canary traffic shift to 0% (rollback traffic), 2) enable fallback routing to v4 for streaming sessions older than 30s, 3) collect full profiler traces from one canary pod, 4) notify CS for customer impact. Executing step 1 now: `redwoodctl traffic update --model model-redwood-5b-v5 --traffic 0 --env canary`

leo: command acknowledged, traffic shift command accepted. rolling traffic back to baseline (v4). Routing policy switched to fallback: `routing:set fallback=redwood-4b stable_only=true`

deploy-bot: Traffic update complete. Canary traffic = 0% as of 11:11 PDT. Fallback routing enabled.

maya: after rollback p95 dropped back near baseline within ~30s. p99 trending down but still elevated for active streams; streaming stalls reduced but not fully cleared for sessions started during canary window.

cs-rep: CS alert: two customers reported slow responses in eng and chat features (session ids shared to SRE). No major data loss; partial degradations. I'm drafting a customer message: short blurb, impacted timeframe 10:45-11:11 PDT, mitigation: rollback to previous model, follow-up once root cause found.

raj: collecting traces now. attaching a small log excerpt from canary pod (`pod-redwood-v5-3`):

```
2026-03-12T10:57:22Z pod-redwood-v5-3 [WARN] kv-cache: miss seq=1145 key=prefix-abc
2026-03-12T10:57:23Z pod-redwood-v5-3 [INFO] batcher: created batch_size=24 wait=214ms
2026-03-12T10:57:23Z pod-redwood-v5-3 [ERROR] streaming: stall detected duration=280ms session=xyz
2026-03-12T10:57:24Z pod-redwood-v5-3 [INFO] model: quant-run q4_0 kernel=matmul_v2
```

emma: looks like quantization kernel path might behave differently with the new tokenizer leading to cache key variance. hypothesis: tokenization or prompt normalization change in v5 -> cache key mismatch -> more full-generation recompute -> batcher pressure -> tail.

leo: can we repro locally with a batch of seqs > 1k and q4_0 path? I'll spin a small perf job against a canary snapshot.

maya: repro job queued: `perf/run --model model-redwood-5b-v5 --seq 1200 --concurrency 8 --quant q4_0`

raj: from quick traces, KV miss -> batcher backlog -> intermittent stalls is consistent. For now mitigation complete (rollback + fallback). Next actions: 1) full perf repro, 2) diff tokenizer behavior v4 vs v5, 3) consider pinning tokenization to stable normalization until v5 fixes, 4) run canary again behind traffic shadowing (no real traffic) once fixed.

cs-rep: customer message posted to impacted accounts. tagging product for external comms.

maya: tagging @emma for follow-through. Also creating a follow-up incident ticket with perf artifacts and repro steps.

raj: handoff to next oncall in ~2h. leaving notes in pager duty and incident doc. If anyone sees p99 bounce back above 0.9s re-alert here. Good job team, we mitigated without major customer outage. :slightly_smiling_face:
